source.title: On damage of interpolation to adversarial robustness in regression

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies interpolation and adversarial robustness in nonparametric regression. Its results do not test the listed versions about in-distribution generalization on natural labels, architecture, optimizer, batch size, regularization, sharpness, or memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on adversarial risk and one standard prediction-risk trajectory. The adversarial results are outside the claim's scope; the standard-risk result does not test any listed version. Cited results from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern interpolation and adversarial risk in nonparametric regression. Its standard-risk experiment varies training epochs at fixed network width. Neither these results nor its theoretical arguments test any listed claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but abbreviated. Under their nonparametric regression assumptions, the authors establish that highly interpolating estimators cannot attain optimal minimax adversarial rates except at sufficiently small attack magnitudes. They also identify regimes where additional samples worsen adversarial risk. Their Auto MPG illustration shows a mild standard-error increase alongside a larger adversarial-error increase, and suggests stopping earlier to optimize robustness.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes minimax adversarial risk for interpolating estimators in nonparametric regression and includes a neural-network training-trajectory illustration; it does not use the original studies' classification generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported results vary with training epoch, input dimension, and adversarial perturbation magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: For the fixed-width Auto MPG network with two predictors, median standard test error increased from 0.595 (0.007) at epoch 30 to 0.681 (0.253) at epoch 1000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard test error can rise mildly during continued neural-network training as training error decreases.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 1–5 establish an additional minimax adversarial-risk cost for highly interpolating regression estimators under the stated distributional assumptions; numerical experiments illustrate this vulnerability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High interpolation can compromise robustness to perturbations of future regression inputs, even where interpolation permits optimal standard-risk rates.

record.problems: The empirical neural-network illustration uses one dataset and reports medians over 100 random train-test splits; the main findings are theoretical and concern adversarial risk rather than the listed in-distribution generalization versions.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4.1 and Figure 3 report adversarial-risk comparisons among regression estimators; Section 4.2 and Figures 4–5 report adversarial risks, dimension comparisons, and optimal epochs. These concern future X-attacks or other measures outside the listed versions, so they were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe; chance-level held-out performance on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning and optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error and interactions with data size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations as predictors of generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Input perturbation robustness is distinct from V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness. The standard-risk theoretical constructions do not test V1's random-label comparison or V2's width dependence. Results outside the versions are already declared in rows_left_out, so no missing claim-relevant rows are required.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label accuracy on classification tasks.
Width sweeps and test error beyond interpolation on MNIST or CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and tuning choices.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: feedforward neural network with three hidden layers of sizes 512, 256, and 128
rows.size_stated: three hidden layers of sizes 512, 256, and 128
rows.stage_stated: trained for up to 1000 epochs using gradient descent with a learning rate of 0.001
rows.operation_detail: Training trajectory on the Auto MPG regression task; reports median standard prediction risk over 100 random train-test splits.
rows.note: Standard risk changes during training, but this regression result does not test any listed version or establish a chance-relative classification result.
rows.check: The subject, condition and numbers match Section 4.2. This is median test squared error across training epochs, which cannot establish any listed version's effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
